input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets our preferred position in full. We may assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate (as defined in § 1.1) or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all assets (24.1); Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld (24.2); Vendor may never assign to a direct Customer competitor (24.2); and our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees or reduce service (24.4). Residual assignments are mutually consent-based with a reasonableness standard (24.3), and § 13 expressly lets us transfer licence rights on a permitted § 24 assignment. Two points short of ideal preferred wording are noted only, not redlined: the reasonableness standard in 24.2 is framed by reference to an assignee with adequate capability and financial standing, and the competitor bar is subject to our own consent — both remain within our control and benefit us. No anti-assignment wording elsewhere (§ 30 General, § 29 Notices) cuts across this.
